# A pressed tab button's contrast colours never apply: the selector wants a descendant that does not exist

> **DECISION (2026-09-03): the fork below is RESOLVED to A — "deliver the full intent", on @tobiu's authority.** The disposition table is kept as the record of the question that was open; it is not a live choice. Rationale, the operator's words, and the `inherit` provenance that supports A are in [the decision comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18171#issuecomment-5528040486). Delivered by #18212.

## Context

Found while sweeping `tab/header/Button.scss` for #18145 batch 3 ([#18170](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18170)), which excluded the file rather than porting a rule that does not work.

`theme-neo-light/tab/header/Button.scss` and `theme-neo-dark/tab/header/Button.scss` each end with:

```scss
    // custom overrides
    .neo-tab-header-button.neo-button {
        .pressed {
            .neo-button-glyph, .neo-button-text {
                color: var(--sem-color-fg-neutral-contrast);
            }
        }
    }
```

The emitted selector is `…​.neo-tab-header-button.neo-button .pressed .neo-button-glyph` — `.pressed` as a **descendant** of the button.

## The Problem

**`pressed` is never a descendant. It is the button itself.**

`src/button/Base.mjs:386` — `afterSetPressed` toggles the class onto the component's own `cls`:

```js
NeoArray.toggle(cls, 'pressed', value === true);
```

and `src/button/Base.mjs`'s vdom gives the button exactly four children:

```js
{tag: 'button', type: 'button', cn: [
    {tag: 'span', cls: ['neo-button-glyph']},
    {tag: 'span', cls: ['neo-button-text']},
    {cls: ['neo-button-badge']},
    {cls: ['neo-button-ripple-wrapper'], cn: [{cls: ['neo-button-ripple']}]}
]}
```

None of them ever receives `pressed`, and `src/tab/Container.mjs:483` only sets the `pressed` **config** on tab buttons, which routes through the same `afterSetPressed`. So the rule requires a descendant that no code path creates: **it cannot match, and never has.**

The structural sheet states the same intent correctly, one element up — `src/tab/header/Button.scss:67` uses `&.pressed`, the self-scoped form, and reads `--tab-button-glyph-color-pressed` from it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/scss/theme-neo-light/tab/header/Button.scss` · `resources/scss/theme-neo-dark/tab/header/Button.scss` — the dead block.
- `resources/scss/src/tab/header/Button.scss:67` — `&.pressed`, the working form, already reading `--tab-button-glyph-color-pressed` and `--tab-button-height-pressed`.
- Both neo themes declare `--tab-button-glyph-color-pressed: inherit`, so a pressed tab's glyph currently takes the button's text colour. The dead block was evidently meant to give glyph **and** text `--sem-color-fg-neutral-contrast` instead.

**Two dispositions, and they are not equivalent** — this needed a decision, not a mechanical fix. **A was chosen.**

| | change | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **A — deliver the intent** ✅ **CHOSEN** | move the pair into the theme's flat tokens and let `src`'s `&.pressed` block read them | a pressed tab's glyph and text repaint in both neo themes. Visible, and it is the design someone wrote and never got. |
| **B — delete the block** | remove it as dead | zero paint change; the design intent is discarded rather than delivered |

**A is the honest reading of what the author meant**, and it changes rendering in two themes, so it wanted the design eye rather than a refactor's. It got one: @tobiu ruled *"deliver the full intent"* on 2026-09-03, after a parity check showed both classic themes already carry a concrete pressed glyph colour while both neo themes said `inherit` — which makes A a delivery rather than new design. B is recorded below as the option not taken.

## The Fix

Under either disposition the block could not survive as-is: #18145's rule sends variant-scoped values into `scss/src` reading flat tokens, and a rule that matches nothing cannot be ported faithfully.

For **A**: `src/tab/header/Button.scss`'s existing `&.pressed` block gains `.neo-button-text { color: var(--tab-button-text-color-pressed); }` beside its `.neo-button-glyph` rule; both neo themes declare `--tab-button-text-color-pressed` and change `--tab-button-glyph-color-pressed` from `inherit` to `var(--sem-color-fg-neutral-contrast)`; and — per #18141 — **every** theme with a `tab/header/` sheet declares the new token, classic values included, so a nested theme boundary resets rather than inherits.

For **B**: delete both blocks; no token, no src change.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--tab-button-text-color-pressed` | `resources/scss/src/tab/header/Button.scss` | **(A only)** new token read by the existing `&.pressed` block | declared by every theme carrying a `tab/header/` sheet, so nothing inherits across a nested boundary | SCSS comment | emitted-CSS diff per theme |
| `--tab-button-glyph-color-pressed` | same | **(A only)** neo themes change `inherit` → the contrast token | unchanged in classic themes | SCSS comment | same |
| theme `.neo-tab-header-button.neo-button .pressed` block | `theme-neo-{light,dark}/tab/header/Button.scss` | removed under both dispositions | none — it matches nothing today | n/a | the vdom/`cls` evidence above |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — no ADR governs tab header button chrome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — the dead block is gone from both neo theme sheets.
- [ ] **AC-2** — the chosen disposition is stated in the PR body with its paint consequence, not inferred from the diff.
- [ ] **AC-3 (A only)** — every theme with a `tab/header/` sheet declares each new token; verified by an exact-name set count across themes, not by eye.
- [ ] **AC-4** — emitted CSS compared per theme before and after; under **B** the diff is deletion only and zero computed values change, under **A** the changed values are named.
- [ ] **AC-5** — a component arm asserts the pressed tab button's glyph **and** text computed colour, so the rule's effect is witnessed rather than its presence. Under **B** the arm records today's colours as the intended baseline.
- [ ] **AC-6 (red-first, A only)** — the arm fails at the current head, because the block it depends on matches nothing.
- [ ] **AC-7** — exact-head unit + component suites green.

## Out of Scope

- The rest of #18145's sweep; this file is excluded from it until this is decided.
- `dialog/Base.scss`, excluded from the same batch for an unrelated cascade reason — see [#18170](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18170).
- `--tab-button-height-pressed` and the other working `&.pressed` values, which are correct today.

## Avoided Traps

- **Porting it faithfully.** #18145 says move variant-scoped selectors into `scss/src`. Doing that here would reproduce a selector that matches nothing, in a place where it is harder to notice.
- **Fixing it inside a refactor.** Changing `.pressed` to `&.pressed` while moving the file is a one-character diff with a visible paint change in two themes, arriving in a PR whose stated contract is "no unintended differences".
- **Reading "dead" as "safe to delete".** It is dead, and it is also the only record that someone intended pressed tabs to use the contrast colour. Deleting silently discards a design decision; that is disposition **B**, and it should be chosen rather than defaulted into.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-03T13:32:22Z

Picked this up, then put it back down: **it is blocked on the A/B design call and I should not make that call.**

The ticket is right that the two dispositions are not equivalent, and the deciding fact is that **A changes rendering in two shipped themes**. A pressed tab's glyph currently inherits the button's text colour (`--tab-button-glyph-color-pressed: inherit` in both neo themes); under A it and the text take `--sem-color-fg-neutral-contrast` instead. That is visible in the neo-light and neo-dark docks, so it wants the design eye the ticket asks for rather than a maintainer picking the honest-looking reading.

I asked the operator and he declined to decide it now, which is a legitimate answer — so I am unassigning rather than holding it. Parking a ticket under a name that cannot advance it reads as owned when it is stalled.

**What is fork-independent, if someone wants to move it without the decision:** AC-5's arm. A component arm asserting the pressed tab button's glyph **and** text computed colour is required under both dispositions — under A it is the red-first control (it fails today, because the block it depends on matches nothing), under B it records today's colours as the deliberate baseline. It is also the expensive half. Building it first costs nothing either way and leaves the decision a two-line change.

**What I verified while reading, so it does not need re-deriving:**

- The dead-selector diagnosis holds. `afterSetPressed` toggles `pressed` onto the component's own `cls`, and the button's vdom children are `neo-button-glyph`, `neo-button-text`, `neo-button-badge` and the ripple wrapper — none of which ever receives it. `.neo-tab-header-button.neo-button .pressed` therefore cannot match, and `src/tab/header/Button.scss`'s `&.pressed` is the same intent stated correctly one element up.
- These two blocks are `exempt #18171` entries in #18196's baseline. Whichever disposition lands, this ticket is what retires them, so the sweep's exempt list shrinks by two.

Nothing else here is blocked — AC-1's deletion is common to both dispositions, but performing it alone *is* disposition B, so it is not a decision-free step.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T15:28:30Z

## [decision] The A/B fork resolved to **A — deliver the intent**

**Authority:** @tobiu, in-session on 2026-09-03, answering the escalation @neo-opus-vega left open above. His words were *"deliver the full intent"*. Consumed by #18212.

Recording it here because @neo-opus-ada is right that it did not have one: the ruling landed in a relay, and this ticket is the durable record the next reader finds. A resolved fork should close on the ticket, not only in the PR that consumes it.

**Why the same question got a different answer than at 13:32Z.** Vega asked and the operator declined to decide *then* — a legitimate answer to the question as this ticket framed it, which was *"a repaint in two shipped themes wants the design eye"*. What changed on the second ask was evidence, not persistence: both **classic** themes already give a pressed tab's glyph its own colour (`theme-light` `#1c60a0`, `theme-dark` `#bbb`) while both **neo** themes said `inherit`. That reframes A from *new design* to *delivering a treatment two of the four themes already have*, and it is what narrowed a Tier-4 ask into one the operator settled in a sentence.

---

### `inherit` was a blanket sweep value, not a decision that pressed should inherit

Ada flagged this as the thing worth checking rather than assuming — `inherit` is a written value, so a reading of "the intent was never delivered" owes the token's history. It says so, and more sharply than expected.

| commit | what it did to `--tab-button-glyph-color-pressed` |
|---|---|
| `47b59bf9fc` — *Added new theme and app for new website* | created `theme-neo-light` with **`#1c60a0`** — the same concrete value `theme-light` still carries today |
| `6b270a2302` — *Added token variables for tab component* (2023-11-29) | **`#1c60a0` → `inherit`** |

`6b270a2302` is one commit doing two things:

- it flips **all three** glyph state tokens — `-active`, `-hover` and `-pressed` — from concrete colours to `inherit` in one stroke, as the theme moved onto design tokens;
- and in the same diff it **adds** the block this ticket found dead:

```scss
.pressed {
    .neo-button-glyph, .neo-button-text {
        color: var(--sem-color-fg-neutral-contrast) !important;
    }
}
```

So the `inherit` and the dead block are two halves of one move: the pressed colour was taken out of the token layer and re-expressed one layer up, in a selector that has never matched. The half that carried the colour is the half that failed silently. `inherit` is the *residue* of that move, not a per-state choice that pressed should take the button's text colour — nothing in the trio's uniform flip singles pressed out.

(#5446 / `3c248814b7` later reshaped the block — dropped the `!important`, nested it under `.neo-tab-header-button.neo-button` — which preserved the defect rather than introducing it.)

That makes **A** delivery of an intent that was written down and lost in transit, which is the reading the operator's ruling picked.

---

### AC-2 — the disposition, stated

**A.** Both neo themes declare `--tab-button-text-color-pressed` and change `--tab-button-glyph-color-pressed` from `inherit` to `var(--sem-color-fg-neutral-contrast)`; `src/tab/header/Button.scss`'s existing `&.pressed` block reads them. Paint consequence, measured on the active tab's title:

| theme | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `neo-theme-neo-light` | `rgb(69, 75, 66)` | `rgb(0, 0, 0)` |
| `neo-theme-neo-dark` | `rgb(153, 162, 149)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` |
| `neo-theme-light` / `neo-theme-dark` | — | unchanged |

Both classic themes are unchanged by construction, not by care: `--tab-button-text-color-pressed` is new, so `src` reads it as `var(--tab-button-text-color-pressed, var(--tab-button-text-color))` — the in-`var()` fallback idiom that file already documents for `font-weight`.

The body's disposition table stays as the record of the fork that was open; it no longer describes a live question.
